ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, when block M is sliding down at a constant speed on a stationary conveyor belt, the conveyor belt suddenly starts rotating clockwise (as shown by the arrow in the figure). After the conveyor belt rotates, how does the friction force on block M change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The friction force on M remains unchanged
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an inclined conveyor belt, lower on the left and higher on the right, with block M placed on the upper inclined section; beside the roller on the right there is an arrow indicating clockwise rotation, and the arrow on the upper section of the conveyor belt points up and to the right along the incline, indicating that when it rotates clockwise, the upper belt surface moves in the uphill direction. Reasoning: When the conveyor belt is not rotating, block M slides down at a constant speed on the stationary belt surface, indicating that the net force along the incline is zero. Therefore, the component of gravity down the incline, mg sinθ, is balanced by the kinetic friction force, whose direction is up along the incline and whose magnitude is equal to mg sinθ, and also equal to μN. After the conveyor belt rotates clockwise, the upper belt surface moves uphill, while the block still has a tendency to slide downward relative to the belt surface / the direction of relative sliding is downward, so the direction of friction is still up along the incline. The magnitude of kinetic friction is μN and does not depend on the relative sliding speed; on the same incline, the normal force N remains unchanged, so the magnitude of the friction force remains unchanged.
